verses.kjv: Then Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.
verses.modern: Then Samuel told the people the rights and duties of the kingship. He wrote them in a book and laid it up before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each one to his home.

verses.kjv: And Saul also went home to Gibeah; and there went with him a band of men, whose hearts God had touched.
verses.modern: Saul also went to his home at Gibeah, and with him went men of valor whose hearts God had touched.

verses.kjv: But the children of Belial said, How shall this man save us? And they despised him, and brought him no presents. But he held his peace.
verses.modern: But some worthless fellows said, "How can this man save us?" And they despised him and brought him no present. But he held his peace.

chapters.summary: Samuel anointed Saul privately and gave him three signs that were fulfilled that day, including prophesying among the prophets. Saul was then chosen publicly by lot at Mizpah, and Samuel presented him to the people as king.

verses.kjv: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabeshgilead: and all the men of Jabesh said unto Nahash, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee.
verses.modern: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and besieged Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Make a treaty with us. We will serve you."

verses.kjv: And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel.
verses.modern: But Nahash the Ammonite said to them, "On this condition I will make a treaty with you, that I gouge out all your right eyes, and so bring disgrace on all Israel."

verses.kjv: And the elders of Jabesh said unto him, Give us seven days' respite, that we may send messengers unto all the coasts of Israel: and then, if there be no man to save us, we will come out to thee.
verses.modern: The elders of Jabesh said to him, "Give us seven days' respite that we may send messengers through all the territory of Israel. Then, if there is no one to save us, we will give ourselves up to you."

verses.kjv: Then came the messengers to Gibeah of Saul, and told the tidings in the ears of the people: and all the people lifted up their voices, and wept.
verses.modern: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul, they reported the news in the ears of the people. All the people wept aloud.

verses.kjv: And, behold, Saul came after the herd out of the field; and Saul said, What aileth the people that they weep? And they told him the tidings of the men of Jabesh.
verses.modern: Now Saul was coming from the field behind the oxen, and Saul said, "What is wrong with the people, that they are weeping?" So they told him the news of the men of Jabesh.

verses.kjv: And the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly.
verses.modern: The Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words. His anger was greatly kindled.

verses.kjv: And he took a yoke of oxen, and hewed them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the coasts of Israel by the hands of messengers, saying, Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen. And the fear of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out with one consent.
verses.modern: He took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, "Whoever does not come out after Saul and Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen!" Then the dread of the LORD fell upon the people. They came out as one man.

verses.kjv: And when he numbered them in Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
verses.modern: When He mustered them at Bezek, the people of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

verses.kjv: And they said unto the messengers that came, Thus shall ye say unto the men of Jabeshgilead, To morrow, by that time the sun be hot, ye shall have help. And the messengers came and shewed it to the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.
verses.modern: They said to the messengers who had come, "Thus shall You say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: 'Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, You shall have deliverance.' " When the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, they were glad.

verses.kjv: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, To morrow we will come out unto you, and ye shall do with us all that seemeth good unto you.
verses.modern: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, "Tomorrow we will give ourselves up to You, and You may do to us whatever seems good to You."

verses.kjv: And it was so on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the host in the morning watch, and slew the Ammonites until the heat of the day: and it came to pass, that they which remained were scattered, so that two of them were not left together.
verses.modern: The next day Saul put the people in three companies. And they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch and struck down the Ammonites until the heat of the day. And those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.

verses.kjv: And the people said unto Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death.
verses.modern: Then the people said to Samuel, "Who is it that said, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Bring the men, that we may put them to death."

verses.kjv: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day the LORD hath wrought salvation in Israel.
verses.modern: But Saul said, "Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel."

verses.kjv: Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.
verses.modern: Then Samuel said to the people, "Come, let us go to Gilgal and there renew the kingdom."

verses.kjv: And all the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal; and there they sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
verses.modern: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they sacrificed peace offerings before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

chapters.summary: Nahash the Ammonite besieged Jabesh-gilead and demanded that every man's right eye be gouged out. Saul rallied all Israel, defeated the Ammonites at the battle of Jabesh-gilead, and the kingdom was renewed at Gilgal.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto all Israel, Behold, I have hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me, and have made a king over you.
verses.modern: Samuel said to all Israel, "See, I have obeyed your voice in all that you have said to me and have made a king over you.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, the king walketh before you: and I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my childhood unto this day.
verses.modern: Now, see, the king walks before you. I am old and gray. See, my sons are with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

verses.kjv: Behold, here I am: witness against me before the LORD, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
verses.modern: Here I am; testify against me before the LORD and before His anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Or whose donkey have I taken? Or whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Or from whose hand have I taken a bribe to blind my eyes with it? Testify against me and I will restore it to You."

verses.kjv: And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man's hand.
verses.modern: They said, "You have not defrauded us or oppressed us or taken anything from any man's hand."

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that ye have not found ought in my hand. And they answered, He is witness.
verses.modern: He said to them, "The LORD is witness against You. His anointed is witness this day, that You have not found anything in my hand." And they said, "He is witness."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto the people, It is the LORD that advanced Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: Samuel said to the people, "The LORD is witness, who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Now therefore stand still, that I may reason with you before the LORD of all the righteous acts of the LORD, which he did to you and to your fathers.
verses.modern: Now therefore stand still that I may plead with You before the LORD concerning all the righteous deeds of the LORD that He performed for You and for Your fathers.

verses.kjv: When Jacob was come into Egypt, and your fathers cried unto the LORD, then the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, which brought forth your fathers out of Egypt, and made them dwell in this place.
verses.modern: When Jacob went into Egypt, and the Egyptians oppressed them, then Your fathers cried out to the LORD and the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt and made them dwell in this place.

verses.kjv: And when they forgat the LORD their God, he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
verses.modern: But they forgot the LORD their God. And He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab. And they fought against them.

verses.kjv: And they cried unto the LORD, and said, We have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD, and have served Baalim and Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve thee.
verses.modern: Then they cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. But now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies. We will serve You.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelled safe.
verses.modern: The LORD sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel and delivered you from the hand of your enemies on every side, and You lived in safety.

verses.kjv: And when ye saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, ye said unto me, Nay; but a king shall reign over us: when the LORD your God was your king.
verses.modern: When You saw that Nahash the king of the Ammonites came against you, you said to me, 'No, but a king shall reign over us,' when the LORD Your God was Your king.

verses.kjv: Now therefore behold the king whom ye have chosen, and whom ye have desired! and, behold, the LORD hath set a king over you.
verses.modern: Now see the king whom you have chosen, for whom you have asked. See, the LORD has set a king over You.

verses.kjv: If ye will fear the LORD, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the LORD your God:
verses.modern: If You will fear the LORD and serve Him and obey His voice and not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, and if both You and the king who reigns over you will follow the LORD Your God, it will be well.

verses.kjv: But if ye will not obey the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then shall the hand of the LORD be against you, as it was against your fathers.
verses.modern: But if You will not obey the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against You and Your king.

verses.kjv: Now therefore stand and see this great thing, which the LORD will do before your eyes.
verses.modern: Now therefore stand still and see this great thing that the LORD will do before Your eyes.

verses.kjv: Is it not wheat harvest to day? I will call unto the LORD, and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the LORD, in asking you a king.
verses.modern: Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call upon the LORD. He will send thunder and rain. And You shall know and see that Your wickedness is great, which You have done in the sight of the LORD, in asking for yourselves a king."

verses.kjv: So Samuel called unto the LORD; and the LORD sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.
verses.modern: So Samuel called upon the LORD. The LORD sent thunder and rain that day. All the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.

verses.kjv: And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto the LORD thy God, that we die not: for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king.
verses.modern: All the people said to Samuel, "Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, that we may not die, for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for ourselves a king."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto the people, Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart;
verses.modern: Samuel said to the people, "Do not be afraid; you have done all this evil. Yet do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all Your heart.

verses.kjv: And turn ye not aside: for then should ye go after vain things, which cannot profit nor deliver; for they are vain.
verses.modern: Do not turn aside after empty things that cannot profit or deliver, for they are empty.

verses.kjv: For the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name's sake: because it hath pleased the LORD to make you his people.
verses.modern: For the LORD will not forsake His people, for His great name's sake, because it has pleased the LORD to make You a people for Himself.

verses.kjv: Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:
verses.modern: Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for You. I will instruct You in the good and the right way.

verses.kjv: Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.
verses.modern: Only fear the LORD and serve Him faithfully with all Your heart. For consider what great things He has done for You.

verses.kjv: But if ye shall still do wickedly, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king.
verses.modern: But if You still do wickedly, You shall be swept away, both You and Your king."

chapters.summary: Samuel gave his farewell address, reminding Israel of God's faithfulness and warning that both they and their king must follow the LORD. He called down thunder and rain in the wheat harvest as a sign, and the people acknowledged their sin in asking for a king.

verses.kjv: Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,
verses.modern: Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,

verses.kjv: Saul chose him three thousand men of Israel; whereof two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in mount Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin: and the rest of the people he sent every man to his tent.
verses.modern: Saul chose three thousand men of Israel. Two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent home, every man to his tent.

verses.kjv: And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebrews hear.
verses.modern: Jonathan defeated the garrison of the Philistines that was at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear."

verses.kjv: And all Israel heard say that Saul had smitten a garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel also was had in abomination with the Philistines. And the people were called together after Saul to Gilgal.
verses.modern: All Israel heard it said that Saul had defeated the garrison of the Philistines, and also that Israel had become a stench to the Philistines. And the people were called out to join Saul at Gilgal.

verses.kjv: And the Philistines gathered themselves together to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea shore in multitude: and they came up, and pitched in Michmash, eastward from Bethaven.
verses.modern: The Philistines mustered to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and troops like the sand on the seashore in multitude. They came up and encamped in Michmash, to the east of Beth-aven.

verses.kjv: When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait, (for the people were distressed,) then the people did hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits.
verses.modern: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble (for the people were hard pressed), the people hid themselves in caves and in thickets and in rocks and in high places and in pits.

verses.kjv: And some of the Hebrews went over Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. As for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
verses.modern: Some Hebrews crossed the fords of the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul was still at Gilgal. All the people followed him trembling.

verses.kjv: And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.
verses.modern: He waited seven days, the time appointed by Samuel. But Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.
verses.modern: So Saul said, "Bring the burnt offering here to me, and the peace offerings." And he offered the burnt offering.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might salute him.
verses.modern: As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived. And Saul went out to meet him and greet him.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash;
verses.modern: Samuel said, "What have you done?" And Saul said, "When I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that you did not come within the days appointed, and that the Philistines had mustered at Michmash,

verses.kjv: Therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication unto the LORD: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.
verses.modern: I said, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal. I have not sought the favor of the LORD.' So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the LORD thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the LORD have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.
verses.modern: Samuel said to Saul, "You have done foolishly. You have not kept the command of the LORD your God, with which He commanded you. For then the LORD would have established Your kingdom over Israel forever.

verses.kjv: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the LORD hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the LORD hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the LORD commanded thee.
verses.modern: But now Your kingdom shall not continue. The LORD has sought out a man after his own heart. The LORD has commanded Him to be prince over His people, because You have not kept what the LORD commanded You."

verses.kjv: And Samuel arose, and gat him up from Gilgal unto Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were present with him, about six hundred men.
verses.modern: Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal. The rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the army; they went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.

verses.kjv: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people that were present with them, abode in Gibeah of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
verses.modern: Saul and Jonathan his son and the people who were present with them stayed in Geba of Benjamin, but the Philistines encamped at Michmash.

verses.kjv: And the spoilers came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned unto the way that leadeth to Ophrah, unto the land of Shual:
verses.modern: Raiders came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned toward Ophrah, to the land of Shual.

verses.kjv: And another company turned the way to Bethhoron: and another company turned to the way of the border that looketh to the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
verses.modern: Another company turned toward Beth-horon. And another company turned toward the border that looks down on the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.

verses.kjv: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears:
verses.modern: Now there was no blacksmith to be found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, "Lest the Hebrews make themselves swords or spears."

verses.kjv: But all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock.
verses.modern: But every one of the Israelites went down to the Philistines to sharpen his plowshare, his mattock, his axe, or his sickle,

verses.kjv: Yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the coulters, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to sharpen the goads.
verses.modern: The charge was two-thirds of a shekel for the plowshares and for the mattocks, and a third of a shekel for sharpening the axes and for setting the goads.

verses.kjv: So it came to pass in the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.
verses.modern: So on the day of the battle there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people with Saul and Jonathan, but Saul and Jonathan his son had them.

verses.kjv: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the passage of Michmash.
verses.modern: The garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

chapters.summary: Saul's son Jonathan attacked the Philistine garrison at Geba, provoking a massive Philistine response. When Samuel delayed coming to Gilgal, Saul unlawfully offered the burnt offering himself; Samuel told him his kingdom would not continue and that God had sought a man after His own heart.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines' garrison, that is on the other side. But he told not his father.
verses.modern: One day Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who carried his armor, "Come, let us go over to the Philistine garrison on the other side." But he did not tell his father.

verses.kjv: And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;
verses.modern: Saul was staying in the outskirts of Gibeah in the pomegranate cave at Migron. The people who were with him were about six hundred men,

verses.kjv: And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD'S priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.
verses.modern: Including Ahijah the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the priest of the LORD in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had gone.

verses.kjv: And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines' garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
verses.modern: Within the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the Philistine garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side and a rocky crag on the other side. The name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

verses.kjv: The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.
verses.modern: The one crag rose on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.

verses.kjv: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.
verses.modern: Jonathan said to the young man who carried his armor, "Come, let us go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. It may be that the LORD will work for us, for nothing can hinder the LORD from saving by many or by few."

verses.kjv: And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.
verses.modern: his armor-bearer said to Him, "Do all that is in Your heart. Do as You wish. See, I am with You heart and soul."

verses.kjv: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.
verses.modern: Then Jonathan said, "See, we will cross over to the men. We will show ourselves to them.

verses.kjv: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.
verses.modern: If they say to us, 'Wait until we come to you,' then we will stand still in our place. We will not go up to them.

verses.kjv: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the LORD hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us.
verses.modern: But if they say, 'Come up to us,' then we will go up, for the LORD has given them into our hand. And this shall be the sign to us."

verses.kjv: And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.
verses.modern: So both of them showed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines. And the Philistines said, "Look, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden themselves."

verses.kjv: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the LORD hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.
verses.modern: The men of the garrison hailed Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, "Come up to us. We will show You something." And Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Come up after me, for the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel."

verses.kjv: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.
verses.modern: Then Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet. his armor-bearer after him. And they fell before Jonathan. his armor-bearer killed them after him.

verses.kjv: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow.
verses.modern: That first strike, which Jonathan and his armor-bearer made, killed about twenty men within about half a furrow's length in an acre of land.

verses.kjv: And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.
verses.modern: There was a panic in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. The garrison and even the raiders trembled, the earth quaked. It became a very great panic.

verses.kjv: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.
verses.modern: The watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and there was the crowd, scattered and going in all directions.

verses.kjv: Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.
verses.modern: Then Saul said to the people who were with him, "Count and see who has gone from us." And when they had counted, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.
verses.modern: Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring the ark of God here." For the ark of God was with the people of Israel at that time.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand.
verses.modern: While Saul was talking to the priest, the tumult in the camp of the Philistines increased more and more. So Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."

verses.kjv: And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.
verses.modern: Then Saul and all the people who were with him rallied and went into the battle. And every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was very great confusion.

verses.kjv: Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.modern: Now the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines before that time and had gone up with them into the camp turned to be with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.

verses.kjv: Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
verses.modern: Likewise, when all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they too followed hard after them in the battle.

verses.kjv: So the LORD saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over unto Bethaven.
verses.modern: So the LORD saved Israel that day. And the battle passed beyond Beth-aven.

verses.kjv: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.
verses.modern: The men of Israel had been hard pressed that day, so Saul had laid an oath on the people, saying, "Cursed be the man who eats food until it is evening and I am avenged on my enemies." So none of the people had tasted food.

verses.kjv: And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground.
verses.modern: Now when all the people came to the forest, there was honey on the ground.

verses.kjv: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.
verses.modern: When the people entered the forest, the honey was dripping, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.

verses.kjv: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.
verses.modern: But Jonathan had not heard his father charge the people with the oath, so he put out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and dipped it in the honeycomb and put his hand to his mouth. His eyes brightened.

verses.kjv: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.
verses.modern: Then one of the people said, "Your father strictly charged the people with an oath, saying, 'Cursed be the man who eats food this day.' " And the people were faint.

verses.kjv: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.modern: Then Jonathan said, "My father has troubled the land. See how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

verses.kjv: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?
verses.modern: How much better if the people had eaten freely today of the spoil of their enemies that they found. For now the slaughter among the Philistines has not been great."

verses.kjv: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.
verses.modern: They struck down the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. And the people were very faint.

verses.kjv: And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood.
verses.modern: The people pounced on the spoil and took sheep and oxen and calves and slaughtered them on the ground. And the people ate them with the blood.

verses.kjv: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the LORD, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.
verses.modern: Then they told Saul, "See, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood." And He said, "You have dealt treacherously. Roll a large stone to me here today."

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the LORD in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.
verses.modern: Saul said, "Scatter among the people and say to them, 'Let every man bring his ox or his sheep and slaughter it here and eat, and do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood.' " So every one of the people brought his ox with him that night and slaughtered it there.

verses.kjv: And Saul built an altar unto the LORD: the same was the first altar that he built unto the LORD.
verses.modern: Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar that He built to the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.
verses.modern: Then Saul said, "Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until the morning light. Let us not leave a man of them." And they said, "Do whatever seems good to you." But the priest said, "Let us draw near to God here."

verses.kjv: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.
verses.modern: Saul inquired of God, "Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel?" But He did not answer Him that day.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Draw ye near hither, all the chief of the people: and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day.
verses.modern: Saul said, "Come here, all you leaders of the people, and know and see how this sin has arisen today.

verses.kjv: For, as the LORD liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.
verses.modern: For as the LORD lives who saves Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die." But there was not a man among all the people who answered him.

verses.kjv: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.
verses.modern: Then he said to all Israel, "You shall be on one side. I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side." And the people said to Saul, "Do what seems good to you."

verses.kjv: Therefore Saul said unto the LORD God of Israel, Give a perfect lot. And Saul and Jonathan were taken: but the people escaped.
verses.modern: Therefore Saul said to the LORD God of Israel, "Give a perfect lot." And Saul and Jonathan were taken, but the people escaped.

verses.kjv: And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.
verses.modern: Then Saul said, "Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan." And Jonathan was taken.

verses.kjv: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die.
verses.modern: Then Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." And Jonathan told him, "I tasted a little honey with the tip of the staff that was in my hand. Here I am; I will die."

verses.kjv: And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.
verses.modern: Saul said, "God do so to me and more also; you shall surely die, Jonathan."

verses.kjv: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.
verses.modern: Then the people said to Saul, "Shall Jonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Israel? Far from it! As the LORD lives, not one hair of His head shall fall to the ground, for He has worked with God this day." So the people ransomed Jonathan. He did not die.

verses.kjv: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines: and the Philistines went to their own place.
verses.modern: Then Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.

verses.kjv: So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them.
verses.modern: When Saul had taken the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, against the Ammonites, against Edom, against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. Wherever he turned he routed them.

verses.kjv: And he gathered an host, and smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them.
verses.modern: He did valiantly and struck the Amalekites and delivered Israel out of the hands of those who plundered them.

verses.kjv: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchishua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:
verses.modern: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-shua. And the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the younger Michal.

verses.kjv: And the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
verses.modern: The name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz. And the name of the commander of his army was Abner the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.

verses.kjv: And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
verses.modern: Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.

verses.kjv: And there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him unto him.
verses.modern: There was hard fighting against the Philistines all the days of Saul. And when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he attached him to himself.

chapters.summary: Jonathan and his armor-bearer attacked a Philistine outpost, and the LORD threw the enemy into a panic, winning the battle of Michmash. Saul's rash oath that no one should eat nearly resulted in Jonathan's death, but the people rescued him.

verses.kjv: Samuel also said unto Saul, The LORD sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the LORD.
verses.modern: Samuel said to Saul, "The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel; now therefore listen to the words of the LORD.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
verses.modern: Thus says the LORD of hosts, 'I have noted what Amalek did to Israel in opposing them on the way when they came up out of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
verses.modern: Now go and strike Amalek and devote to destruction all that they have. Do not spare them, but kill both man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.' "

verses.kjv: And Saul gathered the people together, and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.modern: So Saul summoned the people and numbered them at Telaim, two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.

verses.kjv: And Saul came to a city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley.
verses.modern: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
verses.modern: Then Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, depart; go down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them. For you showed kindness to all the people of Israel when they came up out of Egypt." So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.

verses.kjv: And Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until thou comest to Shur, that is over against Egypt.
verses.modern: Saul defeated the Amalekites from Havilah as far as Shur, which is east of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.
verses.modern: He took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive and devoted to destruction all the people with the edge of the sword.

verses.kjv: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them: but every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.
verses.modern: But Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and of the oxen and of the fattened calves and the lambs. All that was good, and would not devote them to destruction. All that was despised and worthless they devoted to destruction.

verses.kjv: Then came the word of the LORD unto Samuel, saying,
verses.modern: The word of the LORD came to Samuel:

verses.kjv: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king: for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. And it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the LORD all night.
verses.modern: "I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not performed my commandments." And Samuel was angry. He cried to the LORD all night.

verses.kjv: And when Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a place, and is gone about, and passed on, and gone down to Gilgal.
verses.modern: Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning. And it was told Samuel, "Saul came to Carmel, and see, he has set up a monument for himself and turned and passed on and gone down to Gilgal."

verses.kjv: And Samuel came to Saul: and Saul said unto him, Blessed be thou of the LORD: I have performed the commandment of the LORD.
verses.modern: Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed be you to the LORD. I have performed the commandment of the LORD."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
verses.modern: Samuel said, "What then is this bleating of the sheep in my ears and the lowing of the oxen that I hear?"

verses.kjv: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.
verses.modern: Saul said, "They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen to sacrifice to the LORD Your God, and the rest we have devoted to destruction."

verses.kjv: Then Samuel said unto Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what the LORD hath said to me this night. And he said unto him, Say on.
verses.modern: Then Samuel said to Saul, "Stop! I will tell you what the LORD said to me this night." And He said to Him, "Speak."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel, and the LORD anointed thee king over Israel?
verses.modern: Samuel said, "Though you are small in your own eyes, are You not the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed You king over Israel.

verses.kjv: And the LORD sent thee on a journey, and said, Go and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed.
verses.modern: The LORD sent You on a mission and said, 'Go, devote to destruction the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are consumed.'

verses.kjv: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the LORD, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the LORD?
verses.modern: Why then did You not obey the voice of the LORD? Why did You pounce on the spoil and do what was evil in the sight of the LORD?"

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the LORD, and have gone the way which the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
verses.modern: Saul said to Samuel, "I have obeyed the voice of the LORD. I have gone on the mission on which the LORD sent me. I have brought Agag the king of Amalek. I have devoted the Amalekites to destruction.

verses.kjv: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God in Gilgal.
verses.modern: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the best of the things devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD Your God in Gilgal."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
verses.modern: Samuel said, "Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? See, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.

verses.kjv: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
verses.modern: For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and presumption is as iniquity and idolatry. Because You have rejected the word of the LORD, He has also rejected You from being king."

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.
verses.modern: Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.

verses.kjv: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD.
verses.modern: Now therefore, please pardon my sin and return with me that I may worship the LORD."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.
verses.modern: Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you. For you have rejected the word of the LORD. The LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel."

verses.kjv: And as Samuel turned about to go away, he laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent.
verses.modern: As Samuel turned to go away, Saul seized the hem of his robe. It tore.

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto him, The LORD hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.
verses.modern: Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from You this day and has given it to a neighbor of Yours, who is better than You.

verses.kjv: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.
verses.modern: Also the Glory of Israel will not lie or have regret, for He is not a man, that he should have regret."

verses.kjv: Then he said, I have sinned: yet honour me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD thy God.
verses.modern: Then He said, "I have sinned; yet honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, that I may bow before the LORD Your God."

verses.kjv: So Samuel turned again after Saul; and Saul worshipped the LORD.
verses.modern: So Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul bowed before the LORD.

verses.kjv: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.
verses.modern: Then Samuel said, "Bring here to me Agag the king of the Amalekites." And Agag came to him cheerfully. Agag said, "Surely the bitterness of death is past."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
verses.modern: Samuel said, "As your sword has made women childless, so shall Your mother be childless among women." And Samuel hacked Agag to pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.

verses.kjv: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
verses.modern: Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.

verses.kjv: And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul: and the LORD repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.modern: Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, but Samuel grieved over Saul. And the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.

chapters.summary: God commanded Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites, but Saul spared King Agag and the best livestock. Samuel declared that obedience is better than sacrifice, and the LORD rejected Saul as king; Samuel hewed Agag to pieces.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Bethlehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.
verses.modern: The LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you grieve over Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send You to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided for myself a king among His sons."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear it, he will kill me. And the LORD said, Take an heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to the LORD.
verses.modern: Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears it, he will kill me." And the LORD said, "Take a heifer with You and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'

verses.kjv: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will shew thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint unto me him whom I name unto thee.
verses.modern: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice. I will show You what You shall do. And You shall anoint for me Him whom I declare to You."

verses.kjv: And Samuel did that which the LORD spake, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?
verses.modern: Samuel did what the LORD commanded and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city came to meet Him trembling and said, "Do You come peaceably?"

verses.kjv: And he said, Peaceably: I am come to sacrifice unto the LORD: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
verses.modern: He said, "Peaceably; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice." And He consecrated Jesse and His sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the LORD'S anointed is before him.
verses.modern: When they came, He looked on Eliab and thought, "Surely the LORD's anointed is before Him."

verses.kjv: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.
verses.modern: But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not look on his appearance or on the height of His stature, because I have rejected Him. For the LORD sees not as man sees: man looks on the outward appearance. But the LORD looks on the heart."

verses.kjv: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this.
verses.modern: Then Jesse called Abinadab and made Him pass before Samuel. And he said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."

verses.kjv: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this.
verses.modern: Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. And He said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."

verses.kjv: Again, Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, The LORD hath not chosen these.
verses.modern: Jesse made seven of His sons pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, "The LORD has not chosen these."

verses.kjv: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither.
verses.modern: Then Samuel said to Jesse, "Are all your sons here?" And he said, "There remains yet the youngest. But he is keeping the sheep." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and get him, for we will not sit down until he comes here."

verses.kjv: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
verses.modern: He sent and brought Him in. Now He was ruddy and had a beautiful countenance and was handsome. And the LORD said, "Arise, anoint Him, for this is He."

verses.kjv: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
verses.modern: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of His brothers. And the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. And Samuel rose up and went to Ramah.

verses.kjv: But the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him.
verses.modern: Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented Him.

verses.kjv: And Saul's servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.
verses.modern: Saul's servants said to him, "See, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.

verses.kjv: Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.
verses.modern: Let our lord now command your servants who are before you to seek out a man who is skillful in playing the lyre, and when the evil spirit from God is upon you, He will play it, and you will be well."

verses.kjv: And Saul said unto his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.
verses.modern: So Saul said to his servants, "Provide for me a man who can play well and bring him to me."

verses.kjv: Then answered one of the servants, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, that is cunning in playing, and a mighty valiant man, and a man of war, and prudent in matters, and a comely person, and the LORD is with him.
verses.modern: One of the young men answered, "I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, who is skillful in playing, a man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, and a man of good presence. The LORD is with Him."

verses.kjv: Wherefore Saul sent messengers unto Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, which is with the sheep.
verses.modern: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send me David your son, who is with the sheep."

verses.kjv: And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by David his son unto Saul.
verses.modern: Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread and a skin of wine and a young goat and sent them by David his son to Saul.

verses.kjv: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armourbearer.
verses.modern: David came to Saul and entered his service. And Saul loved him greatly. He became his armor-bearer.

verses.kjv: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favour in my sight.
verses.modern: Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my sight."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
verses.modern: Whenever the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, David took the lyre and played it with his hand. So Saul was refreshed and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.

chapters.summary: The LORD sent Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint David, the youngest son of Jesse, as the next king. The Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit troubled him; David was brought to court as a musician to soothe Saul.

verses.kjv: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle, and were gathered together at Shochoh, which belongeth to Judah, and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephesdammim.
verses.modern: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for battle and were assembled at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.

verses.kjv: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and pitched by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
verses.modern: Saul and the men of Israel were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Elah and drew up in line against the Philistines.

verses.kjv: And the Philistines stood on a mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.
verses.modern: The Philistines stood on the mountain on the one side. Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, with a valley between them.

verses.kjv: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
verses.modern: There came out from the camp of the Philistines a champion named Goliath of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.

verses.kjv: And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
verses.modern: He had a helmet of bronze on His head. He was armed with a coat of mail. The weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of bronze.

verses.kjv: And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a target of brass between his shoulders.
verses.modern: He had bronze armor on His legs, and a javelin of bronze slung between His shoulders.

verses.kjv: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver's beam; and his spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.
verses.modern: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam. his spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron. And his shield-bearer went before Him.

verses.kjv: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.
verses.modern: He stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, "Why have you come out to draw up for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

verses.kjv: If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.
verses.modern: If he is able to fight with me and kill me, then we will be your servants. But if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and serve us."

verses.kjv: And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.
verses.modern: The Philistine said, "I defy the ranks of Israel this day. Give me a man, that we may fight together."

verses.kjv: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
verses.modern: When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid.

verses.kjv: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man went among men for an old man in the days of Saul.
verses.modern: Now David was the son of an Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah, named Jesse, who had eight sons. In the days of Saul the man was already old and advanced in years.

verses.kjv: And the three eldest sons of Jesse went and followed Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
verses.modern: The three oldest sons of Jesse had followed Saul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next to him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.

verses.kjv: And David was the youngest: and the three eldest followed Saul.
verses.modern: David was the youngest. The three oldest followed Saul,

verses.kjv: But David went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
verses.modern: But David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.
verses.modern: For forty days the Philistine came forward and took his stand, morning and evening.

verses.kjv: And Jesse said unto David his son, Take now for thy brethren an ephah of this parched corn, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to thy brethren;
verses.modern: Jesse said to David his son, "Take for your brothers an ephah of this parched grain, and these ten loaves, and carry them quickly to the camp to your brothers.

verses.kjv: And carry these ten cheeses unto the captain of their thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge.
verses.modern: Also take these ten cuts of cheese to the commander of their thousand. See how your brothers are and bring some token from them."

verses.kjv: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel, were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.
verses.modern: Now Saul and they and all the men of Israel were in the Valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

verses.kjv: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the trench, as the host was going forth to the fight, and shouted for the battle.
verses.modern: David rose early in the morning and left the sheep with a keeper and took the provisions and went, as Jesse had commanded him. And he came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line, shouting the war cry.

verses.kjv: And Israel and the Philistines had put the battle in array, army against army.
verses.modern: Israel and the Philistines drew up for battle, army against army.

verses.kjv: And David left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage, and ran into the army, and came and saluted his brethren.
verses.modern: David left the things in charge of the keeper of the baggage and ran to the ranks and went and greeted his brothers.

verses.kjv: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.
verses.modern: As he talked with them, Goliath the Philistine champion of Gath came up out of the ranks of the Philistines and spoke the same words as before. And David heard him.

verses.kjv: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.
verses.modern: All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid.

verses.kjv: And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel.
verses.modern: The men of Israel said, "Have you seen this man who has come up? Surely he has come up to defy Israel. And the king will enrich the man who kills him with great riches and will give him his daughter and make his father's house free in Israel."

verses.kjv: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
verses.modern: David said to the men who stood by him, "What shall be done for the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?"

verses.kjv: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that killeth him.
verses.modern: The people answered him in the same way, "So shall it be done to the man who kills him."

verses.kjv: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spake unto the men; and Eliab's anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.
verses.modern: Now Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spoke to the men. And Eliab's anger was kindled against David. He said, "Why have you come down here? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle."

verses.kjv: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause?
verses.modern: David said, "What have I done now? Was it not just a question?"

verses.kjv: And he turned from him toward another, and spake after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner.
verses.modern: He turned away from him toward another, and spoke in the same way, and the people answered him again as before.

verses.kjv: And when the words were heard which David spake, they rehearsed them before Saul: and he sent for him.
verses.modern: When the words that David spoke were heard, they repeated them before Saul. He sent for him.

verses.kjv: And David said to Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.
verses.modern: David said to Saul, "Let no man's heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine."

verses.kjv: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
verses.modern: Saul said to David, "You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are but a youth. He has been a man of war from his youth."

verses.kjv: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock:
verses.modern: But David said to Saul, "Your servant used to keep sheep for his father. And when there came a lion, or a bear, and took a lamb from the flock,

verses.kjv: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.
verses.modern: I went after it and struck it and delivered the lamb out of its mouth. And if it arose against me, I caught it by its beard and struck it and killed it.

verses.kjv: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.
verses.modern: Your servant has struck down both lions and bears, and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God."

verses.kjv: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.
verses.modern: David said, "The LORD who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." And Saul said to David, "Go. The LORD be with you!"

verses.kjv: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.
verses.modern: Then Saul clothed David with his armor. He put a helmet of bronze on his head and clothed him with a coat of mail,

verses.kjv: And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.
verses.modern: David strapped his sword over his armor. And he tried in vain to go, for he had not tested them. Then David said to Saul, "I cannot go with these, for I have not tested them." So David put them off.

verses.kjv: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.
verses.modern: Then he took his staff in his hand and chose five smooth stones from the brook and put them in his shepherd's pouch. His sling was in his hand. He approached the Philistine.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.
verses.modern: The Philistine moved forward and came near to David, with his shield-bearer in front of him.

verses.kjv: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.
verses.modern: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he disdained him, for he was but a youth, ruddy and of a fair countenance.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.modern: The Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

verses.kjv: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.
verses.modern: The Philistine said to David, "Come to me. I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and to the beasts of the field."

verses.kjv: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
verses.modern: Then David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with a sword and with a spear and with a javelin. But I come to You in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom You have defied.

verses.kjv: This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.modern: This day the LORD will deliver You into my hand. I will strike You down and cut off Your head. And I will give the dead bodies of the host of the Philistines this day to the birds of the air and to the wild beasts of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,

verses.kjv: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD'S, and he will give you into our hands.
verses.modern: That all this assembly may know that the LORD saves not with sword and spear. For the battle is the LORD's. He will give You into our hand."

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came and drew nigh to meet David, that David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
verses.modern: When the Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet David, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.

verses.kjv: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
verses.modern: David put his hand in his bag and took out a stone and slung it and struck the Philistine on his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead. He fell on his face to the ground.

verses.kjv: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
verses.modern: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him. There was no sword in the hand of David.

verses.kjv: Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.
verses.modern: Then David ran and stood over the Philistine and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

verses.kjv: And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until thou come to the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.
verses.modern: The men of Israel and Judah rose with a shout and pursued the Philistines until they came to the valley and to the gates of Ekron, so that the wounded Philistines fell on the way from Shaaraim as far as Gath and Ekron.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they spoiled their tents.
verses.modern: The people of Israel came back from chasing the Philistines. They plundered their camp.

verses.kjv: And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; but he put his armour in his tent.
verses.modern: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem. But he put his armor in his tent.

verses.kjv: And when Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he said unto Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son is this youth? And Abner said, As thy soul liveth, O king, I cannot tell.
verses.modern: As soon as Saul saw David go out against the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is this youth?" And Abner said, "As your soul lives, O king, I do not know."

verses.kjv: And the king said, Enquire thou whose son the stripling is.
verses.modern: The king said, "Inquire whose son the boy is."

verses.kjv: And as David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
verses.modern: As David returned from the striking down of the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.

verses.kjv: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, thou young man? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.
verses.modern: Saul said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" And David answered, "I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."
